page0.text:
Going back over a month.
He was summoned to this world before anyone else.

page1.text:
He was not summoned to this country.
A faraway foreign country.
The ground is constantly covered in white, the sky is always gray, and the castle is built hidden in the mountains.

page2.text:
It is always winter in that land.
Coldness and stagnation, barrenness and longing.
They are like living corpses, cutting off their connection with the present world and waiting for a reproduction of a miracle.
The winter coldness takes away their human warmth,
and the stagnant world won't allow them a new lifestyle.
...His family were seekers of the Holy Grail.
Spring won't come for the Einzbern family until the day their dearest wish is fulfilled.

page3.text:
It has already been ten centuries since they started the search for the Holy Grail.
After using every possible method to get close to the Holy Grail, they were eventually able to cast the Holy Grail out of iron.
However, all they could make was the vessel.
No Mystic dwelled within it, and they kept casting vessels that would never be filled.

page4.text:
But, a foreseeable end comes to those days.
They performed a ritual to fill the vessel with the help of outsiders.
The result was both a success and a failure.
The Holy Grail was made.
Through this, the Holy Grail would be filled.
But, it made many enemies at the same time.
Even as the supposed owners of the Holy Grail, they were reduced to mere "providers" of a service, no better than any other mage.

page5.text:
Their tenacity is abnormal.
No. Ever since they almost obtained the Holy Grail a thousand years ago, they had lost their minds.
They broke the rules and constantly pulled the strongest card.
The first time, they did not have the leeway to do so.
The second time, they finally found a loophole in the rules.
The third time, they summoned what they shouldn't have.
Then the fourth time...
They were sure of their victory after gaining the strongest card and its manipulator.

page6.text:
The results were a crushing defeat like never before.
Of all the Servants and Masters, they chose ones who betrayed them.
The man destroyed the Holy Grail, leaving his daughter behind in the winter castle.
They were furious at the man's betrayal and lamented their mistake.
They could not trust outsiders after all.
Only one of their bloodline, their family's creation, who had inherited Magic Circuits perfected over generations, could obtain the Holy Grail.

page7.text:
They had a backup plan to start with.
Then the fifth time...
They made certain they prepared the strongest Master and Servant.
That was him.
Two months before the Holy Grail started.
Every rule was broken for him, Berserker, to be summoned beforehand.

page8.text:
The days that followed were only to hurt the human that would become Master.
...The Command Spell engraved all over the girl's body was only to control Berserker.
It did no good as a Magic Circuit and drained her life away.
Even just a slight move by Berserker would make the girl scream.

page9.text:
It's no wonder.
It was two months until the Holy Grail would appear.
The only thing keeping this great hero in this world was her magical energy and Command Spell.
Berserker was not created from the magical energy of the Holy Grail.
No matter how special she is, keeping Berserker using only her own magical energy is like taking her own life away.

page10.text:
Knowing that, they still did not allow for her to rest.
They abandoned them in the winter forest, filled with a pack of hungry beasts.
They gave them over to the corpses possessed by evil spirits.
They were even thrown into the wasteland where they disposed of their failed experiments.
The only way for the girl to survive was to rely on the giant, the only thing that she had been given.

page11.text:
It was beyond training, it was a fight for survival. Yet the girl survived.
She had the giant attack the oncoming enemies.
Every time, she would let out screams of anguish but had him ceaselessly eliminate everything that attacked.
...He himself does not know...
...when that process became a special one to him.

page12.text:
Despite the girl's young appearance, she hated whining.
Everything that came out of her mouth was an insult.
She must've instinctively known that if she was going to lament, she would become stronger if she hated the cause.
The girl despised Berserker for being ugly and cursed his existence.
It was natural.
The girl would not have to suffer if he had not existed.
She would not have been thrown in such a hell if she had not been chosen as Master.

page13.text:
The girl detested the giant for everything and used him as an outlet for her anger.
The girl got used to controlling Berserker, and by the time the Holy Grail showed signs of its appearance, the pain that attacked her disappeared.
The girl took away reasoning from the giant as if in revenge, treating him as a mute "mad warrior."
...But he already knew that was the girl's utmost resistance.

page14.text:
By doing so, the girl hid her own weakness.
That she could live by herself...
She held her head high since she didn't need any allies that she could trust or friends that she loved.
...That was...
Her way of disguising that she had nothing to call her own.

page17.text:
In the winter forest...
The girl hesitantly touched his arm, stained red from the enemy's blood.
Surrounded by a pack of beasts, the girl braced for death even as she desperately denied it.
At that time...
He was not able to move without an order from his Master, so he was the first to become the beasts' prey.

page18.text:
The pack of beasts pierce his arteries, tendons, and eyeballs with their fangs.
The girl screamed seeing that.
...He couldn't remember what she said then since he had his reasoning taken away.
But the girl screamed not for her sake, but for his.
Even though he destroyed her arm every time he swung his own, she endured it so that he did not die.

page19.text:
That's why both of them were covered in blood.
The giant was covered in the slaughtered beasts' blood, and the girl was covered in her own blood.
...He remembers that winter forest.
The weight of the girl that leaned on him, crying tears of pain.
And he realized.
In that small, cold castle...
The black giant was the only one that the girl talked to.

page20.text:
"No... No, Berserker...!"
She comes into view.
It was the same as that time. The girl is running to him crying, which he had not seen since she had become a Master.
And the man slashes her.
With a horizontal flash, the blond enemy takes away the girl's vision.

page21.text:
Her face is covered in red.
The blind girl runs in spite of that, tripping over rubble.
The slender body falls.
There...
The enemy's sword is swung.

page22.text:
The sword misses her heart.
Her lung must've been pierced, as the girl is coughing up blood, still on the ground.
It is not an instant death.
But, it is fatal.
The girl is left with nothing as her vision is taken away, her lungs are broken, and she even lost her Servant.

page23.text:
If she could die peacefully...
It might at least be a salvation if she could just go to sleep right there.
However...
"...Huh?... It hurts, it hurts, Berserker..."
The girl is moving forward, leaving a trail of blood behind.
She crawls towards the black giant, fumbling and crying in anguish.

page24.text:
How much power was left in him?
He breaks the chains with all his might and grabs at the man.
"...Heh."
The magical spear is thrust.
The spear pierces the giant's heart.

page25.text:
...
And it ends.
The man pulls out the spear as if nothing happened, and the remaining power in the giant completely disappears.

page26.text:
His body disappears.
The power that was giving him form had completely disappeared.
Then, all there is left is for him to disappear.
The Servant lost all his magical energy, and has no power to stay in this world any longer.

page27.text:
He falls to the ground.
But, in his final moment...
He sees the girl fumbling around for him in his peripheral.
...
Strength returns to his collapsing legs.
The law of magecraft that built him,
the regulation of the world that hates inconsistencies,
and the body of rock that crumbles away as sand...

page29.text:
He pushes away every power that tries to eliminate him just with his will.
I can't disappear yet.
He is probably the only one who she could rely on.
In order to support the lonely girl who insulted him, but still believed in him as her only reliance.

page30.text:
"...Where I am I? I don't know, it's so dark I can't tell where I'm going, Berserker..."
With her vision taken away, the girl is crawling with her arms stretched out.
...She must want to feel him, as she cannot see him now.
Her hands covered in blood grope at empty space, trying to verify his existence.

page31.text:
...
There is no power left in him.
There is nothing he can do.
Berserker will fall here and die here.
His body has died, and he has no strength to support his falling body.

page32.text:
It's why I feel safe.
No matter who it is...
I won't lose against them as long as I have you, Berserker...

page33.text:
But not this time.
His mind is dead.
Supporting his body with a mind and a will that should no longer exist, he leaves this world.
His body has not fallen, still invincible.
As if to say that his body cannot give up until the end for the sake of the girl that relies on him.

page34.text:
...And the girl reaches him.
The hand that was only grasping the air finally touches something.

page35.text:
"Oh..."
Coughing up blood, the girl clings onto the hard body.
...She cannot see anymore, but she can still feel him.
Berseker hasn't lost.
She cannot see for herself, but Berserker is strong as always.

page36.text:
"...Yeah. I'm glad. Stay here, okay, Berserker?"
Strength fades from her body.
Everything hurts and she's scared, but it's all right as long as he's here.
He always protected her.
He was scary, but he was really nice.
His big body is like a father's, so she really wanted him to pick her up at least once.

page37.text:
"It's dark but I'm not scared. You're strong, Berserker.
I can be relieved if you stay like this..."
She rests her body on him.
She feels like a hard and big hand is placed on her head.
It's probably true.
He should be patting her head if she opens her eyes.

page38.text:
"...Yeah... It's a bit cold."
Her body is cold.
Recalling the forest from that time, the girl laughs.
It was a long time ago already.
Recalling the giant that protected her even while getting injured, she happily falls and loses consciousness.

page39.text: The man reaches out to the girl in white, who peacefully fell asleep.

page40.text:
"...Stop, you bastard...!!!"
I yell at the top of my lungs.
I don't consider my own danger or what could happen to me.

page41.text:
"...Oh?"
The man stops his arm that he tried to extend.
Behind him is Shinji, surprised at my intrusion.
He smiles ominously.

page42.text:
"Wai..."
My shaky throat speaks before I can think.
However...
There is no way that man will stop.

page43.text:
...
I couldn't even tell him to stop.
The man pulled something out of the girl's body with his bare hands, with a smile still on his face.
A red, dripping object that looks like a fruit.
The thing in the man's hand is, without a doubt, the girl in white's -----.

page44.text:
...
My mind burns down.
I lose my sanity, as fear of being killed and hatred of wanting to kill him gets muddled.

page45.text:
"So we had an audience. I understand how you want to observe my gallant figure, but..."
The man, still holding the red thing in his right hand...
"Know your place. Who do you think you are to order a king, you mongrel!"
He fires one of his countless Noble Phantasms at me.
